questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Haiti?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Haiti article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Haiti?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Haiti on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Haiti article.

questions.proof: The other country on the island is the Dominican Republic.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Haiti?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Haiti article.

questions.proof: Haiti has two official languages: French and Haitian Creole, or "Kreyol", which is a simple version of French mixed with African languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The European Union, _____ and Cuba also give and help Haiti's economy in different ways.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Union”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Haiti article.

questions.proof: The European Union, Venezuela and Cuba also give and help Haiti's economy in different ways.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “This is a religion which came from African folk beliefs in _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “beliefs”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Haiti article.

questions.proof: This is a religion which came from African folk beliefs in Benin.
